title: Ranma ½: Super Indiscriminate Decisive Battle! Team Ranma vs. the Legendary Phoenix (らんま1/2 超無差別決戦! 乱馬チームVS伝説の鳳凰) — Viz: One Grew Over the Kuno's Nest
summary: A 25-minute theatrical short (映連 records 26分), Studio DEEN / Kitty Film, DISTRIBUTED BY TOEI, released 1994-08-20 as one of three shorts in the 「東映アニメスペシャル」 programme alongside GS美神 極楽大作戦!! and 平成イヌ物語バウ 原始イヌ物語バウ — the third and last Ranma film and the only one of the three that adapts the manga (the other two are original screenplays; ja-WP calls them 完全オリジナルストーリー). The premise is verified and the chapter identification holds at both edges: ja-WP's 劇場アニメ list prints 「原作コミックス29巻1、2話」 for this film alone, and the Ranma Wiki's film infobox prints manga = Chapter 301 / Chapter 302, whose scans are filed Vol29Chapter1.png / Vol29Chapter2.png. I read those two scans: the printed pages are headed 「PART.1 恐怖の鳳凰剣」 and 「PART.2 不滅の鳳凰剣」 — the tankōbon numbers chapters PER VOLUME, so the catalog's continuous 1-407 space is a convention, and en-WP's per-volume chapter tables (contiguous 1-407 over all 38 volumes, vol 28 = 290-300, vol 29 = 301-311, sourced to Book Shop Shogakukan ISBN records) convert 29巻1話 → 301 and 29巻2話 → 302. The 新装版 (2002-03) keeps the same boundaries: the publisher's own blurb for 新装版 29 splits the volume 第1話～第2話 (the phoenix chick), 第3話～第7話 (Pink and Link), 第8話 (the oni), 第9話～第11話 (the Kashaō money duel) — en-WP's 301-311 exactly. The film adapts both chapters end to end (the antique-shop purchase and the closing sale of the new egg are both there) and the reverse index closes: of 29 wiki pages that link to the film, only Chapter 301 and Chapter 302 are in the chapter namespace. WHAT MAKES IT MIXED RATHER THAN CANON: beside that complete two-chapter spine sits a large studio-made share — ja-WP says Ryoga, Ukyo and Shampoo, absent from the manga story, are worked in and the phoenix's behaviour is changed so that it attacks everyone indiscriminately; the Ranma Wiki's 24-item difference list adds Ranma's eviction from the Tendo house, the night camped in a vacant lot, Sasuke's errand to Ucchan's and the Cat Café to have the growth pills made, the invented rule that the phoenix re-imprints on a new person every morning (it targets Akane), the five-way aerial assault and the Furinkan rampage; and the distributor's own copy sells the film on it (映連 作品紹介: 「ウッちゃんやシャンプーら、原作に登場しないオリジナルキャラクターが大活躍！」). By my paragraph-level classification of the wiki's scene-by-scene account that is ≈43% studio-made, in two contiguous stretches, in a film whose very title is the original element — a substantial source share beside a substantial original share (Sean 2026-09-05), not the Haruhi shape.

chapters_adapted.note: The Phoenix Sword story, both chapters in full and in order: 301 「恐怖の鳳凰剣」 (vol 29 PART.1 — Kuno buys the egg at the antique shop, Ranma puts it on his head, it hatches and imprints on Ranma as its enemy, Soun's imprinting explanation with the surikogi/surikomi pun, girl-Ranma is attacked twice as hard and the bird is deduced to be female) and 302 「不滅の鳳凰剣」 (vol 29 PART.2 — the shop owner's hundred-year reveal, the Phoenix-Gro growth pills haggled down to ¥100, the feeding battle against Kuno's bokken, the phoenix growing huge, its departure in a blaze of light, and the new egg the owner promptly sells to Kuno again). Both endpoints are the chapters' own: the film opens at Antique Shop Yamatai (ch 301 p. 1) and closes on the egg being bought (ch 302's last page). Only these two chapters: the wiki's reverse index has exactly Chapter 301 and Chapter 302 linking to the film, and no source credits any other chapter. FAITHFULNESS-CLAUSE ALTERATIONS inside the adapted material (divergence, not a second source): Happosai's panty-raid collision that knocks the egg loose in ch 301 becomes a stray baseball; the shop owner sells a RECIPE SCROLL (¥1,000,000 → ¥100) instead of ready-made pills (¥100,000 → ¥100); Ranma's Snake Fist gag that opens ch 302 is cut; Nabiki's 'it must be female' deduction is moved from ch 301 to the film's last scene; Akane douses Ranma instead of Ranma dousing himself; the manga's phoenix only wrecks the park, the film's wrecks the town. This is the ONLY animation of chs 301-302 in the 1989-96 line (the TV run's terminal is ch 229 at ep 161).

position.why: Right on both halves. THE SLOT: the film adapts chs 301-302, seventy-two chapters past the run's honest terminal (ep 161 → END 229), so it sits after the last row on every reading. THE INTRA-SLOT ORDER (161.5 = AniList 1007, the six 1993-94 OVAs; 161.51 = 1008, the two-part SPECIAL; 161.52 = this film): three independent orderings put the film AFTER the SPECIAL and only the air date disagrees. (1) Story order — the SPECIAL adapts 266-278, this film 301-302. (2) Pony Canyon's own DVD: らんま1/2 OVAシリーズ Vol.3 (PCBE-50163, 2001-12-05) lists its 収録内容 as 1 甦る記憶(上) / 2 甦る記憶(下) / 3 超無差別決戦! 乱馬チームVS伝説の鳳凰. (3) Viz numbered the film OVA #9 in its 12-part OVA set, after the SPECIAL's two parts (en-WP; the Ranma Wiki's navigation chain runs Reawakening Memories Part Two → this film → Oh, Cursed Tunnel of Lost Love, which is SUPER Vol.1), and AniList's own relation chain says the same (PREQUEL = 1008, SEQUEL = 1011). Only the calendar dissents: the film opened 1994-08-20, one day after OVA Vol.6 and four months before the SPECIAL's first part. So the stored value is right, though not for the reason its note gives — deriveWatchPosition only sets the .5 (after ep 161) and the 0.01 steps are a collision walk that a stored row then keeps (sync-related-works: 'a wrong intra-slot order is a ruling, never a re-sort'). No correction needed; no ruled position required unless the shelf is ever re-ordered.

repairs.old: Ranma ½: One Flew Over the Kuno's Nest
repairs.new: Ranma ½: One Grew Over the Kuno's Nest
repairs.confidence: high on the fact, YOUR CALL on whether to apply
repairs.evidence: The Viz VHS jacket title is 'One GREW Over the Kuno's Nest' — a pun on the phoenix growing, not on the 1975 film's 'Flew'. en-WP's Ranma episode list cites the jacket directly ('Ranma ½: One Grew Over the Kuno's Nest'. Viz Video. Back of the video (VHS) jacket. ISBN 1-56931-059-9); ANN's encyclopedia entry (anime id 3261, whose plot summary AniList reproduces verbatim) lists 'Ranma ½: One Grew Over the Kuno's Nest' among its alternative titles; the Ranma Wiki carries the box-art image under the same name and its trivia says in as many words that the parody 'has created confusion over the film's English title as One Flew Over the Kuno's Nest'. The stored string is AniList's corrupted form.
repairs.note: OPTIONAL — a display choice, not a data error that breaks anything. The alternative is the literal title both en-WP and ANN use as their primary: 'Ranma ½: Super Indiscriminate Decisive Battle! Team Ranma vs. the Legendary Phoenix'. I propose the one-word fix because it keeps the stored naming convention and removes a documented error.

flags_for_sean: CONFIDENCE IS SPLIT, deliberately. The CHAPTERS are high — four witnesses agreeing at both edges: ja-WP's film list (原作コミックス29巻1、2話), the Ranma Wiki's film infobox (Chapter 301 / Chapter 302) with a closed reverse index (only those two chapter pages link to the film), en-WP's volume-contents tables (vol 28 = 290-300, vol 29 = 301-311, contiguous 1-407 across 38 volumes, matching the stored total), and the printed title pages themselves (PART.1 恐怖の鳳凰剣 / PART.2 不滅の鳳凰剣 — I read the scans). The STANDING is the medium half: no source states one, and this film sits exactly on the canon/mixed line.

THE FORK, one word from you. I ruled MIXED because the studio share is neither small nor cosmetic and it is what the film was sold on: 映連's own 作品紹介 reads 「ウッちゃんやシャンプーら、原作に登場しないオリジナルキャラクターが大活躍！」, ja-WP records that 良牙・右京・シャンプー are worked into a story none of them is in and that the phoenix's habits were changed (in the manga it attacks only Ranma; in the film 狂暴性が増した and it attacks everyone — the premise of the climax), and the film's TITLE is the original element (乱馬チーム). THE COUNTER-READING, which is respectable: nothing in the additions is a second story — the premise, the mechanism (imprinting / the Phoenix Sword), the escalation device (the growth pills), the resolution (the fledging) and the coda (the new egg sold to Kuno) are all the chapters', and every invented scene exists to get the pills made and fed. On that reading this is T28 faithfulness-clause expansion and the row is CANON + divergence (the Haruhi / Mugen Train shape). Either way the chapters, the volume and the position are unchanged — only the label moves.

SIZING (T28) — the method, because no source times the film. (1) DENSITY: the publisher's record for 新装版 29 gives 182 pages over 11 chapters, so chs 301-302 ≈ 33 pages, animated in 25-26 minutes — roughly half the density of the same line's OVA Vol.1 (four chapters, 22巻7-10話, in 30 minutes), i.e. about a 2× stretch. (2) SCENE CLASSIFICATION: I split the Ranma Wiki's scene-by-scene Plot Overview into its 14 paragraphs and classified each against the two chapter summaries and the wiki's own 24-item difference list — ≈57% of the described action is the chapters' own events, ≈43% is studio-made, and the studio material falls in two contiguous stretches: the second act (Akane's failed pill batch → the phoenix rampages in the house → Ranma and Kuno evicted → Sasuke's errand to Ucchan's and the Cat Café → the night in the vacant lot → the morning re-imprinting on Akane) and the climax (the five-way aerial assault, the Furinkan rampage, the Tamanoyu bath-house hot/cold run), plus gag expansions inside adapted scenes (Soun's one imprinting vignette becomes three). Treat the percentage as a proxy with a stated method, not a measurement. (3) The 映連 ストーリー — an industry primary, not a wiki — independently contains the same original block (あかねの調合大失敗 → 天道家を追い出される → 佐助が右京とシャンプーに薬を頼む → 空き地でテント → 刷り込みは目覚める度に替わる).

TASK PREMISE: chapter claim CONFIRMED, one detail REFUTED. It is not a Toho fair — the film was distributed by TOEI (ja-WP 配給: 東映; 映連's record 配給：東映, 製作：小学館/キティ・フィルム/ポニーキャニオン, 映倫番号 26050) and shown in the 「東映アニメスペシャル」 triple bill (en-WP: 'at the Toei Film Festival'). The 'Toho' in the air comes from the Ranma Wiki's film infobox, whose distributor field says Toho — a wiki field lying while the same page's own Releases section says Toei/Shogakukan. Runtime also differs by source: ja-WP and eiga.com say 25分, 映連 says 26分, AniList says 31 — the two Japanese primaries are the ones to trust; the stored ledger does not carry duration, so nothing to repair.

CHAPTER SPACE, stated once for the shelf. The tankōbon do NOT print global chapter numbers — every volume restarts at PART.1 (proved on the page: vol 29's first two title pages read PART.1 / PART.2), which is why ja-WP writes coverage as 「29巻1、2話」. The continuous 1-407 numbering is a convention that en-WP's chapter list, the Ranma Wiki and MangaDex's series record (lastChapter 407) all share and that matches the stored total of 407; I converted through en-WP's volume tables and checked both edges. EDITIONS: 単行本 (少年サンデーコミックス, 38 vols, 1988-04 → 1996-06) and 新装版 (38 vols, 2002-04 → 2003-10) have IDENTICAL volume contents — the publisher blurb for 新装版 29 splits it 第1話～第2話 (the phoenix chick) / 第3話～第7話 (Pink and Link) / 第8話 (the oni) / 第9話～第11話 (the Kashaō vs Nabiki money duel), which is en-WP's 301-311 story for story, and the Ranma Wiki's chapter infoboxes print 'volume 29 (Tankōbon/Shinsoban)'. The 2016-18 少年サンデースペシャル版 (B6, 20 vols) re-splits the same 407 chapters, so a 巻話 form does not carry there — and the Ranma Wiki prints a VIZ volume (27) beside the Japanese one; never read that as the tankōbon number.

WORDING TRAP in two of my sources, recorded so it is not re-discovered as a source claim. The wiki's difference list says 'Sasuke is an anime-only character' and 映連 says 「原作に登場しないオリジナルキャラクター」 of Ukyo and Shampoo — all three are manga characters; both statements mean 'not in THIS story' (chs 301-302). Neither is a claim that the film adapts anything other than the owner's instrument.

ANILIST TAG TRAP, still live on this shelf (from the triage, re-verified here): AniList tags THIS film — the only one of the three that adapts the manga — source null, and tags the two ORIGINAL films (418 Big Trouble in Nekonron, 792 Nihao My Concubine) source MANGA. The tag is wrong in both directions on this owner; never let it decide a bucket.

SHELF ORDERING, a decision bigger than this row. Two of the Ranma post-run works that DO adapt chapters are not on the shelf at all (the triage flagged it): AniList 1011 'Ranma 1/2 SUPER' (287-288, 308, 331-332) and 5493 (悪夢!春眠香, ch 365). If 1011 is ever staged, CHAPTER order and PACKAGING order diverge for the first time — SUPER Vol.1 adapts 287-288, i.e. BEFORE this film's 301-302, while Viz's OVA numbering, Pony Canyon's DVD volumes and AniList's relation chain all put the three SUPER OVAs AFTER it. Today the two agree and 161.52 is right under both; when 1011 lands, pick one rule for the whole block rather than per row.

COVERAGE CONTEXT, outside the ask. This film does not continue the run: the 1989-92 TV series stops at ch 229 (ep 161) and the film starts at 301. Across the whole 1989-96 line the animated blocks after 229 are 230-233 (OVA 1), 241 (OVA 3), 259-265 (OVA 4), 266-278 (the SPECIAL), 287-288 / 308 / 331-332 (SUPER), 301-302 (this film) and 365 (the 2008 short) — so 234-240, 242-258, 279-286, 289-300 and everything from 303 onward except those blocks exist only in print. A viewer arrives at this film having read to ch 300 and resumes at ch 303.

NO ADOPTION, NO OTHER REPAIR. The film's only author link is the standard 原作 高橋留美子 credit on an adaptation of her own chapters — a credit, never a T26 adoption (nothing from the film entered the manga line; the invented material appears in no chapter of 303-407). Stored kind 'movie' is right (a theatrical short with a 映倫 number, Toei-distributed) even though both Viz and Pony Canyon packaged it as the ninth OVA — worth a display label ('film, packaged as OVA 9'), not a kind change. Stored air date 1994-08-20 is confirmed by ja-WP, 映連 and eiga.com.
